player.speaker: Front Commissar
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: János Kovács
line.reaction-briliant.text: The eastern front held, and the factories heard about it. Salgotarjan's workers are arming themselves without waiting for authorisation.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: János Kovács
line.reaction-tactical.text: The front held at a price the industry cannot pay twice. Salgotarjan's output is already falling.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: János Kovács
line.reaction-victory.text: The front has held. Now the miners want to know whether the army is coming to Salgótarján. I need an answer before I go back to the union office.
line.callback-bridgehead.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
line.callback-bridgehead.text: Szolnok is held. The Romanians must now force a river crossing under our guns instead of walking across it.
line.callback-base-taken.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
line.callback-base-taken.text: The military base at Szolnok fell to us with its stores largely intact. The People's Commissariat has stopped rationing small-arms ammunition.
line.callback-reserve-west-vindicated.te: I feared keeping the reserve west would cost us the initiative. It recovered the base and its ammunition. I'll support you if the Council questions the decision.
line.callback-reserve-west-questioned.ro: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-reserve-west-questioned.te: The stores were lost before I released the reserve. You followed my advice in holding it west. I'll explain that to the supply officers myself.
line.callback-reserve-east-vindicated.ro: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-reserve-east-vindicated.te: You sent the reserve east and the bridgehead held. Böhm called it enthusiasm outrunning supply; the result forced the Romanian staff to treat the Tisza as a front instead of a finish line.
line.callback-reserve-east-cost.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
line.callback-reserve-east-cost.text: The bridgehead didn't hold. Those battalions won't be on the relief trains. What can I tell the miners we're sending instead?
line.callback-doctrine-methodical.text: You kept much of the army's equipment in the last operation. I need some of it sent into Salgótarján. The workers are afraid the field formations will stay outside while their streets are attacked.
line.miners-emerge.speaker: János Kovács
line.miners-emerge.text: The men came straight from the pits to the union office for rifles. Some still had their lamps on. I've kept them at the barricades, but that means the furnace crews aren't working. How long must we hold like this?
line.hevesi-opening.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
line.hevesi-opening.text: Salgótarján supplies the coal, steel and railway repairs we need for the next offensive. Its workers have armed themselves. If we leave them without help, I won't get another industrial town to trust our promises.
line.stromfeld-threat.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.stromfeld-threat.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.stromfeld-threat.text: The Czechoslovak columns are closing from three directions. March straight in and we may trap our relief force beside the miners. Break the Kisterenye pincer first, or push gunners and ammunition through now?
line.stromfeld-threat.choice.strike-kist: Concentrate against Kisterenye and break one arm of the encirclement before reinforcing the city.
Gain a prestige award and substantial experience for every core formation, but forgo the two worker battalions.
line.stromfeld-threat.choice.reinforce-w: Push supplies and cadres directly into Salgótarján; the workers must hold while the field units counterattack outside.
Raise two worker battalions and earn their later support, but pay prestige and forgo the core-wide experience award.
line.landler-kisterenye.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.landler-kisterenye.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.landler-kisterenye.text: Break the nearest pincer and keep the road open. Kovács will have to hold without us for those hours. I will put that promise in writing before his battalion returns to the barricades.
line.hevesi-workers.speaker: Gyula Hevesi
line.hevesi-workers.text: The miners will hold the furnaces and railway yards, but they need trained gunners and ammunition more than speeches. Get those through, and they will give you the time to strike outside the city.
line.miner-report.speaker: János Kovács
line.miner-report.text: We can guide you through the cuttings and slag heaps. Some of our companies are still in pit clothes, but they know the ground. What we haven't got is enough trained men for the guns from the depot.
line.stromfeld-final.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.stromfeld-final.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.stromfeld-final.text: Kovács, mark the road from the pits to our guns. Commissar, get it open before his ammunition runs out. Then we can assemble the counterattack at the railway yard.
